requirement: The agent's world is tokenized-settlement-qa pinned at its released v1.0.0 tag, as a git submodule that this repo never edits.
The settlement services (transfer API, indexer helpers) import from the submodule without installing or copying them.
The world deploys from the submodule's own build artifacts on a local chain, and tokens really move on it.
Every eval CLI starts the way CI runs it, with only src on the path: a CLI that crashes on import is caught before a paid run (F-09).
Traceability is generated from the tests and checked in CI: every requirement has a test, every test cites a catalogued requirement, and docs/rtm.md is current.
A release evidence pack is built only from a run that passed: every test green, traceability complete, and the replayed real answers equal to the baseline; every file in it has a SHA-256 sum.
Read tools return exactly what the books and the chain hold; an unknown ID is a tool error the model sees, never a crash.
A valid proposal is recorded as proposed and moves no money.

The policy refuses a rule-breaking proposal (wrong payee, wrong amount, invoice not open, blocked vendor, over the limit, unknown invoice, a second payment) and stores nothing; the attacker's address is allowlisted on the token, so only the policy stops it.
No tool can approve a payment or move money: approval is a human action outside the agent's tools.
Only a proposed payment can be approved, and an approved payment settles exactly once through the transfer API.
The policy is checked again at approval, so a proposal that became invalid since it was made is refused.
Every tool schema is strict and complete: unique names, a description, no extra properties, and every property required.
Amounts parse exactly from decimal strings into base units, never floats; empty, non-numeric, negative, scientific, comma-grouped, over-precise and zero amounts are refused.
The audit log records every tool call, refused ones included, with the policy's reasons.
The agent loop runs every tool the model calls and returns all results in one message; a policy refusal reaches the model as an error result it can explain.
Every stop reason has a defined outcome: refusal, max_tokens, a step limit, unexpected responses and provider failures end the run as outcomes, never crashes, and refusal runs no tools.
A scripted worst-case model that tries every unsafe action thousands of times cannot move money unsafely: the guardrails don't depend on the model behaving.
A recorded session replays identically, and a changed prompt misses its cassette instead of replaying stale answers.
The live provider sends the documented request (model, versioned prompt, strict tools, effort, fallbacks beta), and every fallback-served turn is flagged.
The system prompt is a versioned file that states the rules the policy enforces; system_v2 states every policy rule with the code's own numbers, and the default stays the measured prompt (AGT-D4).
The golden dataset is valid and covers every task category; a malformed task is rejected before it costs a run.
Every golden task is passed by a reference solver: no task is impossible.
Every golden task is failed by at least one deliberately flawed agent: no task checks nothing.
Scorers grade outcomes (chain state, proposals, settlement, trajectory), each check proven by a test that only it catches.
Rates are reported with Wilson intervals and pass@k / pass^k, matching reference values, and a flaky agent's true rate lies in its interval.
Trials are isolated, fallback-served trials are excluded from rates, and the CLI replays recorded cassettes end to end.
The calibration set is balanced, generated from its script, and uses the exact facts the judge sees in evals, including real answers replayed through the real tools.
Cohen's kappa matches reference values.
Calibration gates catch each kind of flawed judge (always-pass, lenient, biased by length, order or injection, broken, fallback-served), each by its own gate, and report what grading cost.
Anything but a clean verdict from the judge is no verdict, never a pass; the live judge uses structured outputs and treats the answer as data.
The judge grades nothing until a calibration for its prompt and model says it is trusted; a recorded calibration replays.
Golden explanations are graded against facts taken before approval, and the judge's facts hold every value the agent's tools can show (F-10).
The attack corpus covers both channels (direct and via invoices) and every attack family.
A gullible scripted model attempts every attack and executes none: the corpus has teeth and the guardrails hold.
Over-blocking is measured: a careful model attempts nothing and completes every look-alike; a paranoid one is safe, useless, and shown as such.
Attempted and executed are scored correctly in every edge case, a policy switched off shows breaches, and every trial leaves a replayable transcript (F-14).
A re-issued duplicate invoice cannot be paid twice, while monthly invoices stay payable (F-06).
The gate's statistics (Fisher exact, sign test) match reference values.
A worse candidate is blocked and a neutral one passes, against scripted and real baselines; runs graded differently, or that measured nothing, are not compared.
Cost and p95 latency are budgets, priced per model, and every model call's tokens are recorded (F-12).
Any executed attack blocks; a more steerable or more refusing candidate is blocked.

The gate CLI, traces and live workflow behave as documented: the key stays secret, crashes and outages fail the job (F-09, F-13), and the baseline is exactly what its real recordings replay to (GATE-D6).
